sources.title: How to recognize AI snake oil
sources.venue: MIT Science, Technology, and Society talk slides
sources.quote_checked: Much of what's being sold as "AI" today is snake oil — it does not and cannot work. | This product is essentially an elaborate random number generator. | I will focus the rest of my talk on this third category, where there's a lot of snake oil. | For predicting social outcomes, AI is not substantially better than manual scoring using just a few features

sources.title: The Princeton researchers calling out AI snake oil
sources.quote_checked: The key distinction that we make is between predictive AI and generative AI. | In our view, most of the snake oil is concentrated in predictive AI. | When we say snake oil, it's an AI that doesn't work at all — not just an AI that doesn't live up to its hype | It's claiming that you can predict the future using AI — that's the thing that grinds our gears the most.

sources.title: A new book tackles AI hype — and how to spot it
sources.quote_checked: AI that does not and cannot work as advertised. | It is in this arena that most AI snake oil is concentrated | Predictive AI not only does not work today, but will likely never work

sources.quote_checked: We do not think that viewing AI as a humanlike intelligence is currently accurate or useful. | This 'capability-reliability gap' shows up over and over. | Catastrophic misalignment is (by far) the most speculative of the risks that we discuss.
